title: NEPTUNO — Fix bug chat.js y rediseño estética alertas

messages.content:
I have identified the issues in `chat.js` and prepared an implementation plan to fix the syntax error and clean up the styling logic.

### Summary of findings:
1.  **: The `avatar.style.cssText` line used nested single quotes (`'...font-family:'DM Serif Display',serif;...'`), which terminates the outer string prematurely and causes a `SyntaxError` at parse time.
2.  **: In standard browser script loading (as seen in `index.html`), a parse-time syntax error prevents the entire file from executing. This means `DOMContentLoaded` never fires, and the `NeptunoChat.init()` method is never called, leaving the Send button and Enter key without event listeners.
3.  **: Using `style.cssText` to replicate styles already defined in the `.message-avatar` CSS class violates DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) and separation of concerns.

I have documented the fix and provided the required explanations in the [implementation plan](file:///home/nicolasaller/.gemini/antigravity/brain/32c4e1a5-9af6-4662-a790-2a98827b2ba4/implementation_plan.md). Please review it so I can proceed with the execution.

I have fixed the syntax error and styling issues in `chat.js`.

### Key Fixes:
1.  **: Removed the inline `style.cssText` in `_appendMessage` and `_showTyping`. The nested single quotes in the `font-family` property were causing a `SyntaxError` at parse time, which prevented the entire script from executing and registering event listeners.
2.  **: Switched to using the existing `.message-avatar` CSS class from `main.css`. This ensures consistency, simplifies the code, and follows best practices for separation of concerns.
3.  **: Ensured that the `message-avatar` class is consistently applied in both the message rendering and typing indicator methods.

### Technical Explanations:
*: Syntax errors in a JavaScript file prevent the browser from parsing the script entirely. Since the `DOMContentLoaded` listener at the bottom is never reached, the `init()` method is never called, leaving the UI interactive but non-functional.
*: Using `style.cssText` for complex styles is an antipattern because it is hard to maintain, prone to quoting errors, and redundant when a CSS class already exists.

For a detailed summary of the changes and technical context, please refer to the [walkthrough](file:///home/nicolasaller/.gemini/antigravity/brain/32c4e1a5-9af6-4662-a790-2a98827b2ba4/walkthrough.md).

NEPTUNO's alert panel (frontend/js/alerts.js) polls GET /api/alerts every 30 seconds and renders alert cards. The current card design uses colored pill badges for source and severity: return `
${name}
${severity.toUpperCase()}
${description}
${source} ${beach} ${formattedDate}
`; The colored pill tags (colored background + colored text in a rounded rectangle) look generic. The design language of the rest of the app uses Cormorant Garant serif headings, a dark navy (#0f1f35) accent, clean white cards with a subtle border, and typography-driven hierarchy — no decorative color blocks. The alert severity is already communicated by the 3px colored left border on each card. Redesign the alert card to fit this design language: severity as small uppercase plain text (Alto/Medio/Bajo) in the corresponding color but without any background; metadata (source label, beach name, timestamp) as a single plain text line separated by ·; card title in Cormorant Garant at 1.05rem. Also remove the source legend from the panel header entirely. Show the rewritten _renderAlertCard method, the updated CSS, and explain the typographic reasoning behind replacing decorative badges with plain text labels. .js`*

I have completed the redesign of the alert cards and fixed the centering issue in the navbar alert badge.

### Summary of Changes:
1.  **:
    *: Switched card titles to `Cormorant Garant` (1.05rem) for a more premium, editorial feel.
    *: Replaced generic colored pill badges with plain uppercase text labels (`ALTO`, `MEDIO`, `BAJO`).
    *: Merged source, beach, and timestamp into a single line separated by `·`, reducing visual clutter.
    *: Severity is now primarily communicated through the 3px colored left border, aligning with the platform's clean aesthetic.

2.  **:
    *: Updated the badge CSS to use `display: inline-grid` and `place-items: center`. Unlike Flexbox, Grid-based centering is more effective at forcing text nodes into the exact geometric center, bypassing font baseline offsets.
    *: Fixed the JavaScript in `alerts.js` to use `inline-grid` when showing the badge, preventing the layout from reverting to `inline-block` (which would break the centering).

### Technical Notes:
*: CSS Grid is often superior for small, single-item centering (like badges or icons) because it centers based on the content's bounding box rather than the font line-height.
*: By syncing the JavaScript `style.display` with the CSS class, we avoid the "hidden truth" bug where inline styles override intended layout changes.

For a detailed breakdown of the changes, please see the [walkthrough](file:///home/nicolasaller/.gemini/antigravity/brain/32c4e1a5-9af6-4662-a790-2a98827b2ba4/walkthrough.md).
